blocks.content: Quiz: Which of the following is true for the HTML id attribute?
Tap an option below to answer:
We use the id attribute to uniquely identify a group of HTML elements.
The id attribute uniquely identifies a single HTML element.
The id attribute uniquely identifies a single HTML element.
We use the id attribute to uniquely identify a single HTML element.
The id attribute uniquely identifies a single HTML element.
The id attribute uniquely identifies a single HTML element.
The id attribute doesn't specify an element's class. We use the class attribute for this, which we will learn next.
Adding styling to a specific element is one of the uses of id.
Adding styling to a specific element is one of the uses of id.
To provide a descriptive name for an input field.
The id attribute's main purpose is not to provide a descriptive name for an input field, although it could be used in relation to label for that use.
The id attribute's main purpose is not to provide a descriptive name for an input field, although it could be used in relation to label for that use.
